correctness.rationale: Natural order forbids nontrivial zero sums; no zero divisors makes nonzero support a Boolean semiring homomorphism on finite valuations. Saturating a classical extension-preserved finite witness r-fold yields a formula valued only in 0 or the maximal t. This gives numeric extension preservation. Semiring Sigma_n equivalence on canonical 0/1 literal annotations would imply forbidden classical finite Sigma_n equivalence. The published Dawar–Sankaran hierarchy is a named premise, not independently reproved. Capped semirings satisfy natural order, semiring identities, positive products and r=k saturation. The standalone exact arithmetic checker passed 2,024 algebra triples and 83,688 formula evaluations; computations do not prove arbitrary n or semiring size. Sources: Brinke–Dawar–Grädel–Pago, arXiv:2605.10829v1, §§2, 5, 8, https://arxiv.org/html/2605.10829v1; Dawar–Sankaran, arXiv:2007.05459v2, §§1, 3–4 and Theorem 4.1, https://arxiv.org/html/2007.05459v2.

originality.rationale: The 2026 full text establishes positive finite preservation for non-Boolean lattice/min-max semirings and a negative result for the infinite natural semiring, not a uniform capped natural semiring hierarchy. The 2020 full text gives the Boolean classical hierarchy but no preservation of quantitative semiring valuations. The new saturation transfer connects them for a concrete non-lattice three-element semiring and all k,n; the published published-finding corpus findings searched do not imply it. Older Boolean-support folklore or other indexed literature may still overlap.
residual_risks: A pre-2026 semiring or database-provenance paper could state an equivalent saturation-to-Boolean transfer theorem under different terminology.
The classical hierarchy is a published deep theorem imported rather than reproved; if its hypothesis or prefix convention changed, the transfer conclusion would need corresponding revision.
The full text of all earlier semiring literature was not exhaustively surveyed; no global novelty certificate is asserted.

value.rationale: The 2026 primary work explicitly identifies finite semiring extension-preservation as an algebra-sensitive frontier and proves finite validity for the three-element min-max lattice semiring. This theorem identifies a natural three-element capped-counting nonlattice semiring with the opposite behavior, uniformly across every fixed existential-first prefix level, and supplies a reusable structural saturation criterion. The all-k,all-n scope and sharp same-cardinality algebra contrast are mathematical content beyond a textbook manipulation or isolated example. Limits: not an exhaustive classification and dependent on the classical finite hierarchy.
